---
title: "Under the hood"
description: "How the Claude suggestion workflows work, step by step, and which R function does what."
---

This page is for anyone who wants to know what the
[roxygen](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and [test](test-suggest.qmd) suggestion
workflows actually do — to trust a suggestion, to adjust a setting, or to
debug a run. You don't need it to use them.

Two principles run through both workflows:

- **Claude returns fields, R builds the result.** Claude never writes a
  finished roxygen block or `test_that()` call. It fills in a fixed form
  (a *tool call*: title, parameters, test assertions, a reason for each
  change, …), and R functions check those fields and assemble the file.
  So Claude can't break the file format, drop a tag, or skip the reason.
- **Nothing is proposed unchecked.** R filters every change by its stated
  reason ([what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed)), and
  every new or changed test is run before it is proposed.

All R code lives in
[`R/functions/`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/tree/main/R/functions)
— in `shared/` and one folder per workflow —
one function per file; the entry scripts `R/suggest_roxygen.R` and
`R/suggest_tests.R` only connect them.

## The workflow around the R script

Both workflows share the same frame. Only the R script in the middle
differs.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  subgraph prep ["Prepare"]
    direction LR
    trig(["PR, schedule<br/>or manual run"]) --> files["Choose files"]
    files --> setup["Install R and your<br/>package's dependencies"]
    setup --> token["Get a short-lived<br/>Claude token"]
  end
  subgraph run ["Suggest"]
    direction LR
    script["R script: review<br/>with Claude, write files"] --> push["Get a push token<br/>(GitHub App)"]
    push --> commit["Commit to a<br/>bot-suggest/ branch"]
    commit --> pr["Suggestion PR +<br/>comment on your PR"]
  end
  prep --> run
```

| Step | Done by | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Choose files | workflow step (shell) | In a PR: the `R/*.R` files the PR changed. In a sweep: all of them (roxygen), or the recently changed ones plus a rotating share (tests, see [sweep scope](test-suggest.qmd#sweep-scope)). Writes `files_to_check.txt`; with no files, all later steps are skipped. |
| Claude token | [`anthropic-token`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/tree/main/.github/actions/anthropic-token) action | Trades GitHub's identity token for a short-lived Claude token, see [Claude setup](claude-setup.qmd). |
| R script | `R/suggest_roxygen.R`, `R/suggest_tests.R` | Everything below. Rewrites files in place and lists them in `updated_files.txt`; writes the PR description (`suggestion_report.md`) and the summary line (`suggestion_summary.md`). |
| Push token | [`resolve-push-token`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/tree/main/.github/actions/resolve-push-token) action | A GitHub App token, so your required checks run on the suggestion PR. |
| Commit and PR | [`commit-updated-files`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/tree/main/.github/actions/commit-updated-files) action | Commits exactly the listed files, opens or updates the suggestion PR, and comments on your PR. See [how suggestions work](suggestions.qmd). |

## Roxygen suggestions

Settings are read once; then each file goes through the same steps.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  subgraph once ["Once per run"]
    cfg["① Load settings"]
  end
  subgraph each ["For each file"]
    direction LR
    parse["② Read the function<br/>and its block"] --> ask["③ Ask Claude"]
    ask --> thr["④ Apply the<br/>threshold"]
    thr --> build["⑤ Build the<br/>new block"]
    build --> write["⑥ Write the file"]
    ask -. "no changes needed" .-> skip(["File left as is"])
    thr -. "nothing accepted" .-> skip
  end
  subgraph after ["After the last file"]
    report["⑦ Write the report"]
  end
  once --> each --> after
```

### ① Load settings

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`resolve_shared_path()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/resolve_shared_path.R) | Finds a settings or prompt file: your repository's own copy if it has one ([override](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance)), otherwise the shared one. |
| [`read_json_config()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_json_config.R) | Reads a JSON settings file, e.g. the style guide `config/roxygen-style.json`. |
| [`read_text_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_text_file.R) | Reads the prompt template `prompts/roxygen-review-prompt.md`. |
| [`read_package_name()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_package_name.R) | Reads the package name from `DESCRIPTION`. |
| [`find_study_group()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/find_study_group.R) | DataSHIELD clients: finds the demo-server study group that fits this package, for ready-made login examples. |
| [`build_demo_login_snippet()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/build_demo_login_snippet.R) | DataSHIELD clients: builds the multi-study login code to use in `@examples`. |
| [`role_guidance()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/role_guidance.R) | DataSHIELD: picks the client or server guidance (e.g. about disclosure control) and adds the login example. |
| [`build_role_guidance_text()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/build_role_guidance_text.R) | Turns that guidance from the settings file into a paragraph for the prompt. |

The Claude settings (model, `accept_reasons`, …) come from
`config/claude.yml`, profile `roxygen-review`.

### ② Read the function

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`parse_r_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/parse_r_file.R) | Finds the first function in the file, its parameters and the roxygen block above it, with every tag and its lines. |
| [`select_profile()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/select_profile.R) | Picks the style guidance for an exported or an internal function (by `@export`). |
| [`fn_source()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/fn_source.R) | Cuts out the function's source code, so Claude can check the documentation against it. |

### ③ Ask Claude

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ask_claude_for_review()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/ask_claude_for_review.R) | Prepares and sends the review request; returns Claude's fields. |
| [`build_guidance_text()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/build_guidance_text.R) | Turns the style guide's per-tag rules into a list for the prompt. |
| [`fill_template()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/fill_template.R) | Fills the prompt template's `{{PLACEHOLDERS}}` with the function, its block and the guidance. |
| [`build_submit_review_tool()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/build_submit_review_tool.R) | Defines the form Claude fills in: one field per documentation part and parameter, a list of changes with a reason each, and possible code bugs. |
| [`suggestion_reasons()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/suggestion_reasons.R) | The fixed list of reasons Claude may give (`missing`, `inaccurate`, `incomplete`, `clarity`, `style`). |
| [`call_claude_tool()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/call_claude_tool.R) | Sends the request to the Claude API and returns the filled-in form; stops with a clear error if the answer was cut off or refused. |

### ④ Apply the threshold

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`accepted_roxygen_fields()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/accepted_roxygen_fields.R) | Keeps a change only if its reason is accepted and the text really differs (more than whitespace, punctuation or case). Records applied and dropped changes for the report. |
| [`original_roxygen_field()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/original_roxygen_field.R) | The current text of one documentation part, for the comparison. |
| [`implicit_roxygen_field()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/implicit_roxygen_field.R) | The same for a title or description written without a tag (the first lines of the block). |
| [`roxygen_field_text()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/roxygen_field_text.R) | Claude's new text for one documentation part. |

### ⑤ Build the block and ⑥ write the file

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`build_roxygen_block()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/build_roxygen_block.R) | Assembles the new block in the configured tag order: accepted parts from Claude, all other lines and tags (`@export`, `@seealso`, …) exactly as they were. |
| [`strip_artifact_lines()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/strip_artifact_lines.R) | Removes stray `#'` or `@tag` lines Claude might have copied into a field; an empty required field stops the file instead of breaking it. |
| [`write_in_place()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/write_in_place.R) | Replaces the old block with the new one in the file. |

### ⑦ Write the report

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`format_roxygen_summary()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/format_roxygen_summary.R) | The summary line, e.g. "8 changes applied · 3 not applied · 1 possible bug". |
| [`format_roxygen_report()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/format_roxygen_report.R) | The suggestion PR's description: applied changes per file, not applied ones per reason with Claude's proposed text. |
| [`format_code_issues()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/roxygen/format_code_issues.R) | The "Possible bugs in the code" section. |
| [`comment_once()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/comment_once.R) | Without a suggestion PR: posts the possible bugs as a comment on your PR, but not again on the next push. |

## Test suggestions

The test workflow adds two things the roxygen workflow doesn't need: it
**runs tests** — before and after Claude's changes — and it deals with
**existing tests**, not only new ones.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  subgraph once ["Once per run"]
    cfg["① Load settings,<br/>describe the test data"]
  end
  subgraph prep ["For each function: ask"]
    direction LR
    read["② Read the function<br/>and its test file"] --> base["③ Run the existing<br/>tests, get the history"]
    base --> ask["④ Ask Claude"]
  end
  subgraph verify ["For each function: verify"]
    direction LR
    check["⑤ Check the<br/>answer"] --> cand["⑥ Write and run<br/>a candidate"]
    cand --> keep["⑦ Keep only<br/>what passed"]
    cand -. "new test failed" .-> classify["⑧ Ask Claude why"]
  end
  subgraph after ["After the last function"]
    fin["⑨ Set up testthat if needed,<br/>write the report"]
  end
  once --> prep --> verify --> after
```

### ① Load settings and describe the test data

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`resolve_shared_path()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/resolve_shared_path.R), [`read_json_config()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_json_config.R), [`read_text_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_text_file.R), [`read_package_name()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/read_package_name.R) | As for roxygen: settings, prompts and the package name. Claude settings come from the `test-review` profile in `config/claude.yml`. |
| [`test_support_files()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/test_support_files.R) | Lists your `tests/testthat/setup*.R` and `helper*.R` files — where logins, fixtures and helpers live. |
| [`summarize_test_data()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/summarize_test_data.R) | Describes the test data those files create, so Claude can check concrete values; never fails the run. |
| [`collect_test_data()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/collect_test_data.R) | Does the actual work in a separate R process: loads your package, runs the support files, and lists each table's rows, columns, types, missing values and factor level counts (also tables inside a DSLite server). |

### ② Read the function and its test file

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`parse_r_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/parse_r_file.R) | Finds the function and its name, as for roxygen. |
| [`find_existing_test_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/find_existing_test_file.R) | Looks for `tests/testthat/test-<function>.R`. |
| [`parse_test_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/parse_test_file.R) | Finds the `test_that()` blocks in it, and marks which ones can be safely edited (unique name, own lines). |
| [`detect_dslite_setup()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/detect_dslite_setup.R) | DataSHIELD clients: checks whether your support files already start a DSLite test server. |
| [`build_test_role_guidance()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/build_test_role_guidance.R) | The testing strategy for the prompt: the default one, or for a DataSHIELD client one that uses its existing DSLite setup — or, without one yet, the DSLite datasets Claude can choose from. |

### ③ Run the existing tests and collect the history

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`run_test_blocks()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/run_test_blocks.R) | Runs a test file with your package loaded from source and reports each test as passed or failed, with the error. |
| [`format_test_results()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/format_test_results.R) | Turns those results into lines for the prompt. |
| [`build_test_evidence()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/build_test_evidence.R) | From git: when the function and its test last changed, and in a PR whether the function changed without its test, with the diff. Helps Claude tell an outdated test from a bug. |

### ④ Ask Claude

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ask_claude_for_tests()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/ask_claude_for_tests.R) | Prepares and sends the request: function, test file, support files, test data, test results and history. Returns Claude's fields. |
| [`format_test_support_files()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/format_test_support_files.R) | Puts your support files into the prompt word for word, so the tests use your own objects and helpers. |
| [`fn_source()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/fn_source.R), [`fill_template()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/fill_template.R) | As for roxygen: the function's code, and filling the prompt template. |
| [`build_submit_tests_tool()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/build_submit_tests_tool.R) | Defines the form: new tests (description, reason, setup code, assertions — at most `max_new_tests`), decisions on existing tests, and the DSLite dataset if one is needed. |
| [`suggestion_reasons()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/suggestion_reasons.R) | The fixed list of reasons for new tests (`uncovered_branch`, `error_handling`, `edge_case`, `regression`, `other`). |
| [`call_claude_tool()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/call_claude_tool.R) | Sends the request to the Claude API, as for roxygen. |

### ⑤ Check the answer

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`filter_generated_tests()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/filter_generated_tests.R) | Keeps a new test only if its reason is accepted, its name isn't taken, and its assertions aren't already in the file. |
| [`review_existing_tests()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/review_existing_tests.R) | Checks Claude's decisions on existing tests against the safeguards: the reason fits the action, only a failing test is updated, a possible bug is only reported. |
| [`assemble_test_block()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/assemble_test_block.R) | Builds the `test_that()` code from Claude's fields — the only place test code is assembled. |
| [`strip_artifact_lines()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/strip_artifact_lines.R) | Removes stray code fences Claude might have put into a field. |
| [`ensure_dslite_setup_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/ensure_dslite_setup_file.R) | DataSHIELD clients without a DSLite setup: writes `setup.R` (or `setup-dslite.R`) with the dataset Claude chose. |
| [`build_dslite_test_snippet()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/build_dslite_test_snippet.R) | The DSLite login code for that file. |

### ⑥ Write a candidate and run it, ⑦ keep what passed

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`rewrite_test_content()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/rewrite_test_content.R) | Builds the test file from the original: updates in place, deletions removed, new tests appended, every other line unchanged. |
| [`write_test_file()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/write_test_file.R) | Writes the file — or puts it back exactly as it was when nothing is kept. |
| [`run_test_blocks()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/run_test_blocks.R) | Runs the candidate file. The final file is then rebuilt from the original with only the tests that passed. |

### ⑧ Failed new tests

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ask_claude_to_classify_failure()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/ask_claude_to_classify_failure.R) | Shows Claude the failed test and its error output and asks why it failed: `real_bug`, `bad_test` or `env_misconfiguration`. Uses its own profile, `test-failure-classification`. |
| [`build_submit_failure_classification_tool()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/build_submit_failure_classification_tool.R) | The form for that answer: one of the three categories, plus an explanation. |
| [`create_bug_issue()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/create_bug_issue.R) | `real_bug`: opens an issue, which outlives the PR. |
| [`post_test_failure_comment()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/post_test_failure_comment.R) | The other two, in a PR: a comment on your PR. |
| [`format_test_failure()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/format_test_failure.R) | The text of that comment — or, in a sweep, an entry in the report. |

### ⑨ Set up testthat and write the report

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ensure_testthat_setup()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/ensure_testthat_setup.R) | If new tests were kept: creates `tests/testthat.R`, adds `testthat` to `Suggests`, and sets edition 3 for a fresh setup — so R CMD check runs the tests. |
| [`format_test_summary()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/format_test_summary.R) | The summary line, e.g. "7 new tests · 1 existing test updated". |
| [`format_test_report()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/format_test_report.R) | The report: changes to existing tests, tests to look at, and in a sweep the failed tests — grouped per test file. |
| [`publish_test_report()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/tests/publish_test_report.R) | Puts the report into the suggestion PR's description; without one, a comment on your PR, or in a sweep one issue. |

## Shared helpers

Used by both workflows (and partly by [DESCRIPTION authors](authors-suggest.qmd),
which doesn't use Claude).

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`report_style()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/report_style.R) | Reads the report layout from `config/report-style.yml` (heading sizes, spacing). |
| [`report_heading()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/report_heading.R) | A section heading of a report, e.g. "Applied changes (8)". |
| [`report_groups()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/report_groups.R) | The collapsible groups in a report, e.g. one per file. |
| [`get_github_json()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/get_github_json.R) | Reads from the GitHub API; a failure skips that item instead of stopping the run. |
| [`post_github_json()`](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/blob/main/R/functions/shared/post_github_json.R) | Writes to the GitHub API (comments, issues); a failure is logged, not fatal. |
